neighbours.label: the subject of a popular-history or prehistory narrative: historical figures, groups and creatures being reconsidered (dinosaurs, Lincoln, the pilgrims, the Donner Party)
fire: A new study suggests that the dinosaurs may have been in decline long before the asteroid struck.
Historians still argue about whether Lincoln planned emancipation from the very start of the war.
Every schoolchild learns how the pilgrims survived their first harsh winter in Massachusetts.
The museum's new hall shows how the mammoths roamed the frozen plains of Siberia.
A recent biography claims that Washington was far more anxious than his portraits suggest.
Researchers now believe the Vikings reached North America centuries before Columbus.
The diaries reveal how the settlers crossed the mountains in the brutal winter of 1846.
Fossil footprints show that the sauropods travelled in herds across the ancient floodplain.
quiet: A new study suggests that the smartphones in our pockets may be harming our sleep.

A recent profile claims that the chief executive is far more anxious than interviews suggest.

notes: Card top examples: dinosaurs, Lincoln, pilgrims, sauropods, 'Before Columbus', Donner Party, all in pop-history/news-about-history prose. Near misses keep the news/popular-science register but the subject is modern.
